relevance_note: Case report of one man with familial LCAT deficiency: "Sanger sequencing identified the patient was heterozygous for c.560T>C p.(Leu187Pro) and c.809C>T p.(Thr270lle)"; his sister carries c.560T>C.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. Three people: the proband ('patient', single case-report patient) and his two sisters ('The patient has 2 sisters: one with LCAT deficiency, the other asymptomatic.'), labelled 'sister of patient' (the affected one, mentioned first) and 'sister of patient 2' (the unaffected one who came forward as donor and carries c.560T>C). No variant row for the affected sister: the paper gives her a diagnosis but ties no LCAT variant to her. The unaffected sister's zygosity is not stated; the proband's VUS classification was not copied to her row. The proband's protein change is printed 'p.(Thr270lle)' (lowercase 'll'), kept verbatim. The paper says 'heterozygous for' both variants; phase/compound heterozygosity is not stated, so zygosity is recorded as 'heterozygous'. Biopsy findings come from the Supplementary Figure S1 legend ('Renal biopsy results from patient taken in 2019'), which is in the Footnotes and supplement. 'Foamy material within the lumen' was not taken as glomerular foam cells; 'renal scarring' was not taken as glomerular sclerosis. 'No CER or LCAT activity' is a plasma assay of the patient, not recorded as variant functional evidence and not mapped to 'reduced cholesteryl ester fraction'. Lipids (triglycerides, cholesterol, unesterified-to-total ratio) are reported only as changes with PLEX or in figures, so lipid checklist items other than LpX are not reported. The hedged statement that PLEX 'may have caused acute tubular necrosis' was not recorded. The sister's 'no stigmata of FLD' is too general to exclude any specific checklist item; her 'normal renal function' was used to exclude chronic kidney disease or renal failure. Vital status 'alive' is inferred from 'Currently, he is listed for deceased donor kidney transplantation'. No contradictions found.
